split_question: Should the UK pay for full membership of the EU's next research programme, even if it means cutting other science spending?
angles: join in full and cut other science budgets to pay
join only the Excellent Science part and keep the rest at home
join in full but negotiate a stricter refund rule and find new money
facts_for_writers: The UK has not committed to joining FP10 but has budgeted £2.2 billion a year, roughly what it spends on the current programme (s1).
Science Works projects a £7.7 billion shortfall over FP10's life, up to £16.5 billion in the worst case; the most likely gap is £1.2 billion in 2029-30, rising to £1.5 billion by 2034-35 (s1).
Science Works says joining only the Excellent Science part would cost £2.4 billion a year less than full membership and free about £1.1 billion a year for British priorities (s1).
The UK is currently refunded when its grants underperform by 16%, while Switzerland's trigger is 8%; Science Works suggests negotiating a higher trigger if the UK joins in full (s1).

The 2025 spending review provided for a UK contribution at roughly current levels, to be reviewed once more information was available; the UK joined Horizon in 2023 and has done strongly in the European Research Council and Marie Curie grants (s2).
